questions.q: What does idempotent mean for a pipeline job?
options: Running it twice gives the same result as running it once
It runs only once per day
why: Speed is a different property.
Correct. This makes retries and backfills safe.
Idempotent jobs can fail. They are safe to retry.
The schedule is not the point.

options: ETA shown to a customer after they place an order
why: Weekly plan can be a batch table.
A report can be a batch job.
Correct: a person waits and the newest data matters.
Yearly budget is a slow planning task.

questions.q: Which are valid retraining triggers? (pick all)
options: Live MAE above a limit for 3 days
Input feature distribution shifted a lot
The data scientist feels like it
why: Time-based trigger.
Performance-based trigger.
Drift-based trigger.
A good pipeline uses rules that can be checked and logged.

questions.q: Scenario: your backfill for last month gives different forecasts than the original runs, with the same model. What is the most likely cause?
options: The job reads 'latest' data instead of data as of the run date
Time zones were wrong in the model
why: CPU does not change results this much.
Correct: the inputs have changed since then (late data, corrections), so the job is not reproducible.
Possible but not the most likely cause.
The scheduler product does not change the numbers.

questions.q: Scenario: the nightly job fails at 03:00 and planners start at 07:00. What is the best fallback?
options: Leave the table empty and alert
Serve yesterday's forecast or a seasonal naive forecast, and alert
why: An empty table stops the business.
Correct: a simple but valid forecast is better than none. Also tell the team.
Endless retries can overload the system.
The business cannot wait.

questions.q: In a test, the error for 'retrain every 7 days' is 4.5 and for 'every 1 day' it is 4.2. The retrain job costs 10 times more per day than per week. What does this suggest?
options: Weekly may be enough, because the gain from daily retraining is small
why: The gain is only 0.3 for a much larger cost.
Correct: compare the benefit of lower error with the cost of the extra runs.
Old models grow worse over time.
That is much longer and the error would be larger.
